clue.text: Company exhibition stall shouldn't give way when taken

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a stand is a booth at a trade exhibition

explanation.surface: A company's stall at a trade show must stay upright once it has been booked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a resolute position you take, and once taken it should not yield.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolute position is one that, once adopted, is meant to hold against pressure.

clue.text: Perfect! The pack is mine!

explanation.surface: A card player gleefully claims the deal as the perfect outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as a card player saying 'I deal', the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect means flawless or model; a player who has the pack in hand announces 'I deal'.

clue.text: Your humble servant turned in, turned out lame

indicators.note: turned out signals that the letters of the words in and lame come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A humble servant who went to bed emerged limping.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'turned' only paints the surface (turned in, gone to bed); 'turned out' rearranges IN and LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a lowly domestic worker, a humble servant.

clue.text: Give a sound good mark for getting through the Entrance

indicators.note: a sound of something is how it is said, so the spoken phrase is spelt as another word

parts.note: giving it a good mark means to tick it, a check mark on work

explanation.surface: Someone is told to award a solid good mark for passing an entrance exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a good mark' is to TICK IT; said aloud it is the word entered. 'Give a' completes that phrase around 'sound', which signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass or admission slip is what lets the holder through the door of an event.

clue.text: First night, very jittery

indicators.note: First asks for the opening letter of the word night
jittery suggests shaking, so the letters of very are jumbled

explanation.surface: An actor on opening night is very jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening N, then VERY rearranged as ERVY; the whole clue paints a first-night performer on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nervy means being edgy and anxious, as performers are at a premiere.

clue.text: That upsetting feeling when one goes into the red?

definitions.text: That upsetting feeling when one goes into the red?

parts.words: That upsetting feeling when one goes into the red?
parts.note: an upset is a fall, and going into the red at the bank wipes out what was in the account

explanation.surface: The dismay of an overdrawn account.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses: falling over (being upset) and a bank account that no longer holds money once overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Toppling over is a physical failure of equilibrium, and an overdraft means the account's sum has gone.

clue.text: A toff losing weight over an important matter of separation

parts.note: someone losing weight is reducing, or slimming
a toff is a gentleman, shortened to gent

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman on a diet takes priority over a crucial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: In chemistry, substances such as carbon reduce metal ores, separating the metal from oxygen; 'over' puts REDUCING above A GENT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists use a substance that removes oxygen to extract metals from their ores.

clue.text: Golf and football manoeuvres suggesting something underhand

parts.note: a hole is the unit of play on a golf course
taken as written
a corner is a set play in football, a corner kick

explanation.surface: Tactics on the golf course and the football pitch hint at something shady.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase pictures hiding away in holes and corners, hence secretive dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done furtively, out of sight, is secretive and deceitful.

clue.text: What The Arrow meant for Robin?

definitions.text: What The Arrow meant for Robin?

parts.words: What The Arrow meant for Robin?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Who Killed Cock Robin, the sparrow shot the bird with a bow and arrow, aiming at the bird's chest

explanation.surface: A question about the target of an archer's arrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The British nursery rhyme 'Who Killed Cock Robin?' has the sparrow shoot the robin with an arrow; the robin is known for its red chest, and the word is also a name for the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin's familiar orange-red chest gives the bird a common name.

clue.text: Not so hot here as there, but Daisy shed shift

definitions.text: Not so hot here as there

indicators.note: shift tells us to move the letters of Daisy and shed around

explanation.surface: A gardener moves the daisy shed out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a flower or a name but is pure fodder with 'shed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a street or garden out of the sun is cooler than the sunny part.

clue.text: Please, quietly go and disperse for the rest of the canvassing work

indicators.note: disperse means scatter, so the remaining letters are rearranged
go tells the letter for quietly to leave the word

parts.note: p (piano) is the music abbreviation for quietly

explanation.surface: Canvassers are politely asked to keep quiet, scatter and rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from PLEASE leaves LEASE, which 'disperse' rearranges. 'Canvassing' is a pun on painting on canvas, not on electioneering.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holds the canvas, a rest for painting work.

clue.text: A man in earlier days

parts.note: a grown man was once a lad, and his early life is his time as a young person

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a man as he was long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both a young man and the early period of life, which a man looks back on.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lad, and also the period of being young, both describe a man's early years.

clue.text: Light filters for the blind

parts.note: a venetian window covering is made of thin strips that let some daylight through

explanation.surface: A charity provides light-filtering aids for people who cannot see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blind' looks like people without sight; it is a window covering.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin horizontal strips of a venetian window covering control how much light comes in.

clue.text: A spirited horse finds way over rising river

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for the river is read upwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A lively horse finds a route across a river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' sets ST above the reversed river in the down entry; DEE turned gives EED.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount, especially a lively riding horse, is poetically called this.

clue.text: Prospero's sprite receives radio, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for what picks up radio is sounded out

parts.note: an aerial is an antenna that picks up radio signals

explanation.surface: The magician's airy servant picks up radio broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: Prospero is the magician in Shakespeare's The Tempest; his spirit servant's name sounds like a radio antenna.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Tempest the airy spirit serving Prospero bears this name.

clue.text: A shipwreck can he the making of a N, African cavalryman

indicators.note: wreck means to wreck or break up, so the letters of a ship are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shipwreck might make a man of a North African horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipwreck' looks like one word but splits: SHIP is fodder and 'wreck' the anagram signal on A SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Spahis were Algerian and other North African light horsemen in the French army.

clue.text: Struggle with blows to get where the refreshments are

explanation.surface: Elbowing one's way to the food table at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Pronounced differently: to batter about, and a table laid with food.
explanation.definitionFit: To batter is to strike repeatedly, while a self-service spread of food is laid on a table.

clue.text: The age where one comes to a full stop

explanation.surface: Someone describes an era as the point where everything halts.
explanation.walkthrough: An era of history, and the American word for the punctuation mark that ends a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or epoch, and also the dot that ends a sentence.

clue.text: I laze uneasily and from the sound of it do little on the stage!

definitions.text: from the sound of it do little on the stage

indicators.note: uneasily suggests restless movement, so the letters of I laze are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy actor lounges about, barely acting.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl of Shaw's play Pygmalion; 'from the sound of it' turns 'do little' into her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's flower-seller heroine in Pygmalion has the surname Doolittle.

clue.text: Please, come to order or slip away

indicators.note: come to order means the letters of please are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A chairman begs a meeting to come to order before it drifts off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please, come to order' reads like a chairman's call; it rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes, goes by unnoticed.

clue.text: Burns celebration dish, silver, breaks into reflective sigh

indicators.note: breaks into puts the silver symbol inside the reversed word
reflective means the word sigh is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Burns Night dish served on silver prompts a thoughtful sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns Night is the Scottish celebration of poet Robert Burns. SIGH reversed is HGIS, broken by AG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish pudding of offal and oats is the centrepiece of a Burns Night supper.

clue.text: I held wild Indian territory with capital

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of I held are scrambled

explanation.surface: A ruler boasts of having held a wild Indian region.
explanation.walkthrough: It is both a territory of India and the city housing India's capital, New Delhi.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian national capital territory contains New Delhi, seat of government.

clue.text: A decamper's stretch?

parts.note: someone who decamps literally leaves camp, so the canvas shelter is no longer theirs

explanation.surface: A question about the distance covered by someone who has fled.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word: ex-tent, a former shelter for someone who has broken camp; and it means range or stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or scope is a stretch, and broken into two the word is a former canvas shelter.

clue.text: How he laughs at a signal to work!

definitions.text: How he laughs at a signal to work!

parts.words: How he laughs at a signal to work!
parts.note: a person who laughs scornfully hoots, and factory sirens once sounded to call shifts

explanation.surface: A lazy worker laughs at the factory whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: It is one who hoots with laughter and the factory siren that signals a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory siren calling workers, and a person who laughs loudly or derisively.

clue.text: Big stick wielded for those on roll

explanation.surface: A big stick is brandished at the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A long pole, and the people on an organisation's payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking pole or rod, and the employees of an organisation.

clue.text: Swoon without much distinction

explanation.surface: Someone collapses unremarkably.
explanation.walkthrough: To pass out, and the adjective meaning dim or barely visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out briefly, and also dim or barely perceptible.

clue.text: People can't get out and about when they are cold and old

definitions.text: People can't get out and about when they are

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
aged means old

explanation.surface: Older people stay indoors when it's cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold and old' reads like the elderly stuck indoors in winter; they are C and AGED, describing being locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals behind bars cannot roam freely, being confined.

clue.text: Leave the vehicle before goods put aboard

indicators.note: before puts the vehicle ahead of the word for leave in the entry

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go means to leave

explanation.surface: Get out of the vehicle before the goods are loaded on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight loaded onto a ship or plane is the merchandise carried.

clue.text: Knocked out by chance, apparently it's always happening!

parts.note: an accident is a chance event
someone knocked out lies flat, face down

explanation.surface: Someone flattened by sheer chance seems to have mishaps constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: ACCIDENT ('chance') then PRONE ('Knocked out'); 'by' links them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who constantly suffers mishaps is described as liable to them.

clue.text: Announce the chamber to be reserved for a higher class of traveller

definitions.text: to be reserved for a higher class of traveller

parts.note: to state is to announce
a room is a chamber

explanation.surface: A notice declares the first-class cabin booked.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the private cabin on a ship or train kept for first-class passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A private cabin on a liner or sleeping car is kept for first-class passengers.
